question: If the perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 36 units, then its area is (in square units):
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the equilateral triangle = Perimeter ÷ 3 = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 units.

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × (side)²

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 144 = 36√3 square units.

**∴ The correct answer is 36√3 square units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ba0ba256c6c5775cf9b507fc067924fee8169c0272afa86dcb6f862857ae72c.png] 

**Given:**

Perimeter of the equilateral triangle = 36 units

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of an equilateral triangle = 3 × a (where 'a' is the side length)

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 × a = 36

⇒ a = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 units

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 12²

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 144

⇒ Area = 36√3 square units

**∴ The correct answer is 36√3 square units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Altitude of an Equilateral Triangle

The height (or altitude) of an equilateral triangle is given by h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a, where 'a' is the length of the side.

Inradius and Circumradius

For an equilateral triangle, Inradius (r) = a ÷ (2√3) and Circumradius (R) = a ÷ √3. The ratio of the circumradius to the inradius is always 2:1.

Area of an Isosceles Triangle

Area = (b ÷ 4) × √(4a² − b²), where 'a' is the length of the two equal sides and 'b' is the base.
